analysis: The PR's only change is a documentation edit in docs/developer/test.md, around head line 1049-1050: the SDK 27 release-qualification text now says SDK 27.2 / Swift 6.4.2 (Xcode 27.2) with a link to the build guide's release toolchain section. That hunk lies beyond the two supplied excerpts (lines 1-927), so I could only check it through the patch excerpt. No code, configuration, key handling, authorization, attestation, encryption or cache behavior changes. The visible head text is existing test guidance. It stresses isolated state (Never point tests at production; isolated ephemeral caches, 'Never use production cache roots/keys'; DARKBLOOM_SSD_TEST_TMPDIR rejecting symlink, relative and missing paths). It also states the evidence limits of CPU tests: they prove API wiring, not native capabilities or hardware qualification. Nothing there weakens the T-041 cache mitigations (HMAC names, TTL, KEK purge) or the logout/endpoint-resumption statements in the logout/resumption table. The toolchain bump affects the build supply chain, but the build.md anchor and any CI/toolchain pin changes are outside the supplied evidence. They are an unverified contract rather than a finding. The doc does not change the threat model's trust boundaries or assumptions.
